findings.body:
**`src/ops/fix/report.ts:254-255`: `unresolved` counts skipped rows, which the same file defines as resolved.**

The doc comment at Lines 99-108 says `skipped` rows are "resolved without an attempt by an earlier verified sibling". It also says `unresolved` "counts every row still needing work". The code computes `unresolved` as `rows.length - fixed`. `fixed` requires `commits.length > 0`, so every skipped row (outcome `fixed`, no commits) is counted as unresolved. This makes `planned = fixed + skipped + unresolved` impossible.

Any consumer that treats `unresolved > 0` as outstanding work will report work for a run whose rows are all resolved.

Also, `skipped` does not check `attempts.length === 0`, although the doc says "without an attempt". A `fixed` row with attempts and no commits is counted as both `attempted` and `skipped`.

If the current formula is intentional, change the doc to say so. If it is not, apply this fix:

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-  const fixed = rows.filter((row) => row.outcome === 'fixed' && row.commits.length > 0).length;
+  const fixed = rows.filter((row) => row.outcome === 'fixed' && row.commits.length > 0).length;
+  const skipped = rows.filter(
+    (row) => row.outcome === 'fixed' && row.commits.length === 0 && row.attempts.length === 0,
+  ).length;
   return {
     planned: rows.length,
     attempted,
     fixed,
-    skipped: rows.filter((row) => row.outcome === 'fixed' && row.commits.length === 0).length,
-    unresolved: rows.length - fixed,
+    skipped,
+    unresolved: rows.length - fixed - skipped,
```
</details>
